# AI Bot prioritises lives — intake brief

## Problem statement

The attract/demo bot (`createCompetentBotBrain`, driven by `PlayScene` in demo
mode) treats **Extra Life** as just another power-up. It therefore ignores the
single most valuable outcome in the run — preserving the ship — when a life is
under-capped, and it never steers deliberately toward an Extra Life drop on the
screen. When the hold-full choice opens, the bot auto-selects the **first**
option regardless of what is offered, so an offered Extra Life is frequently
passed over.

## Users

- **Player / operator watching attract mode** — wants the demo bot to play
  credibly, i.e. to value survival and to pick up lives when it can.

User stories:

- As a player watching attract mode, I want the demo bot to take an Extra Life
  offer in the hold-full selection when it is below the life cap, so the demo
  looks like a competent player.
- As a player watching attract mode, I want the demo bot to divert to an Extra
  Life drop that is on screen when it is below the life cap, so it does not
  squander a free life.

## Users / stakeholders

- **AI Bot** (the demo/attract bot) is the actor whose behaviour changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Hold-full choice prefers Extra Life.** When the hold-full choice
  offers `extra_life` and the bot's lives are below the cap (`5`), the bot
  selects the `extra_life` option (demo mode). When `extra_life` is not offered,
  or lives are at the cap, the existing auto-select behaviour is unchanged.
- **AC2 — On-screen Extra Life is prioritised.** While a live `extra_life` drop
  is on screen and the bot's lives are below the cap, the bot's chosen target is
  that drop (subject to the survival tier — the bot never trades its life for a
  life). At the life cap the drop receives no special priority.
- **AC3 — Life cap is single-sourced.** The life status used by the bot
  (`lives`, cap) is derived from the existing game data (GDD cap `5`,
  `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.extra_life.livesMax`); no new magic `5` is introduced.
- **AC4 — Gym↔game parity preserved.** The change lives in shared code
  (snapshot/world/model/goal content or shared choice policy) and the
  duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and gym-parity docs
  assertions still pass; any gym that exercises drop collection or the
  hold-full choice sees the same behaviour.
- **AC5 — Test coverage.** Unit tests cover: (a) the choice policy selects
  `extra_life` when offered and lives < cap, and falls back otherwise;
  (b) the drop-target priority puts an on-screen `extra_life` first when
  lives < cap and does not when at the cap; (c) survival still dominates the
  life preference.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, and the GDD
  attract/demo subsection where it describes bot priorities.
- **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (typecheck,
  lint and build included).

## Constraints

- The demo bot is the shipped AI Bot; behaviour is only observable in demo
  mode, so the change must not alter normal (human) play, including the
  non-demo hold-full selection which must keep waiting for a real selection.
- Survival is a hard constraint above every other tier — the life preference
  is only ever applied when the bot can safely take it.
- Keep the 5-life cap consistent with the GDD (§3.1 / §4.5) and the Extra Life
  catalogue entry.
- No new magic numbers outside the existing bot tunables module(s).

## Existing state

- Demo bot: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` → `botBrain = createCompetentBotBrain()`,
  decisions from `buildBotSnapshot(this)` (`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts`).
- `BotSnapshot` currently has **no life state** — `lives` is not exposed, so the
  decision layer cannot see the life count today.
- Priority bands (`src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts`): survival >
  minerals > power-ups > enemies > asteroids. `extra_life` already has the
  highest power-up value (`1.5`, `src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts`), but
  minerals are a higher band, so minerals currently outrank an Extra Life drop.
- Hold-full choice: `PlayScene.openMineralChoice()` launches
  `MineralChoiceScene` with `options`; in demo mode it passes
  `autoSelectMs = BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`, and the overlay then does
  `this.select(0)` — always the first option (`src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`).
- Cap constants: `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.extra_life.livesMax = 5`
  (`src/powerups/types.ts`); GDD §4.5 caps lives at 5.

## Desired change

1. Expose the bot's life state on `BotSnapshot` (lives + cap, or a derived
   `livesBelowCap` boolean) via `buildBotSnapshot`, read from the scene's run
   state.
2. Add a **secure-life** behaviour to the competent bot that targets a live
   `extra_life` drop when lives < cap, placed as the highest band below
   survival (above minerals). At the cap, the drop falls back to its existing
   power-up band.
3. In demo mode, make the hold-full auto-selection prefer the `extra_life`
   option when offered and lives < cap, otherwise keep the existing
   first-option behaviour.
4. Update docs and tests as above.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — Add life state (`lives`, cap / `livesBelowCap`) to
  `BotSnapshot`, read from the scene's run state.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — Add the `secure-life` priority band
  below survival and above minerals; keep content-adaptive registration.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — Collect behaviour reuse for the
  life target.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts` — Reference the Extra Life cap /
  fallback value.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — Any new tunable (single source).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Pass bot life state into the snapshot; choose the
  preferred demo option for the hold-full choice.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — Accept a preferred demo selection index
  (instead of hard-coded `0`).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — Only if the choice/collection path is
  shared there (parity).
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Document the life
  priority.
- Tests: `src/ai/framework/competent/*.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The life cap is `5` (GDD / `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.extra_life.livesMax`).
- **Assumption:** The change targets the demo/attract bot (`PlayScene` demo
  mode). Normal player selection is never auto-driven.
- **Assumption:** "Prioritise lives" means Extra Life outranks minerals and all
  other power-ups when it can be safely taken and lives < cap. If the operator
  intended a weaker preference (Extra Life above other power-ups but below
  minerals), revisit AC1/AC2.
- **Assumption:** At the life cap the Extra Life drop receives no special
  attention (collecting it is wasted).
- **Risk — survival regression:** diverting to a life must not bypass the
  survival tier. Mitigated by keeping the new band strictly below survival.
- **Risk — parity drift:** bot/choice logic duplicated between game and gym
  would trip the duplicate-body guard. Mitigated by placing logic in shared
  core/competent modules.
- **Risk — scope creep:** "make the bot better at survival generally" is out of
  scope; record any such ideas as linked work items.
- **Assumption:** The legacy `botDecision.ts` heuristic is not the live demo
  brain (`PlayScene` uses the competent brain); if it is still consumed
  elsewhere, mirror the life preference there for consistency.

## Related work

- AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB — Demo bot: human-like input limits and complete the
  hold-full upgrade choice (added the demo auto-select; this extends it).
- AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L — Demo bot movement goals: minerals > power-ups >
  enemies > asteroids (priority bands; this adds a life band).
- AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4 — Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester
  telemetry (the competent brain this changes).
- AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ — Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic.
- AH-0MTVYCM2N002NKE4 — Player pickup pickups as soon as they touch.
- AH-0MUNS3VAQ0023L1J — Increase the probability of lives powerup being spawned.
- AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3 — Add an extra life power up.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — competent bot goals/behaviours and priority bands.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §3.1 / §4.5 — lives model and cap.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should an on-screen Extra Life outrank minerals, or only other power-ups,
  when the bot has fewer than 5 lives?" — Answer (intake agent, documented
  assumption; seed intent "prioritize lives" read as strongest non-survival
  priority): "Outrank minerals when lives < cap; ignore at cap." Source: seed
  intent `AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4`. **OPEN QUESTION** for producer: confirm this
  interpretation.
- Q: "What is the life cap?" — Answer: `5`, from the GDD §4.5 and
  `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.extra_life.livesMax`. Source: repo search.
- Q: "Does this affect human play?" — Answer: "No; the auto-selection change is
  demo-only, matching AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB · AC5." Source: existing behaviour.
- Q: "Which bot does the demo use?" — Answer: the competent framework brain
  (`createCompetentBotBrain`) wired in `PlayScene`. Source: repo search.


## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTCNZX16007ECPS** – Power-up catalogue + effects (P5, P8, P9) (completed)
- **AH-0MUL0WS9P006NUCT** – enemy-configs.csv working-tree change removes header and trailing newline (fails csv-seed tests) (completed)
- **AH-0MUYOBU4F003EYRP** – [test-failure] src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts > Demo mode integration (AH-0MUX496TY005FF3P) > AC1 — the demo bot drives the ship through the live shared input path — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: bot, choice, extra, full, hold, hull, intent, lives, offered, one, pick, pickups, prioritize, screen, seed, selection, should, take, there, they, try
- `README.md` — matched: bot, choice, extra, full, hold, hull, intent, lives, offered, one, pick, pickups, screen, seed, selection, should, take, there, they, try
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: bot, choice, extra, full, hold, hull, lives, one, pick, screen, seed, should, take, there, they, try

# Single enemy gym scene with in-panel enemy selector dropdown

## Problem statement

The dev gym index currently renders **one ENEMIES row per `EnemyConfig`**, each
booting the same reusable `GymEnemies` scene with a fixed `{ enemyKey }`. To
compare archetypes a designer must return to the index, and the column grows
with every "Save As…" entry. There is no way to switch the active enemy type
from inside the scene. We want **one** enemy gym scene with an in-panel
dropdown that swaps the active enemy type live.

## Users

- **Game designer / developer tuning enemy formations, shots and visuals.**
  - As a designer, I want a single enemy gym scene where I can pick any
    (non-boss) enemy from a dropdown, so that I can switch archetypes in one
    place without going back to the index.
  - As a designer, I want choosing an enemy to immediately clear the scene and
    spawn that enemy type, so that what I see always matches the selection.
  - As a designer, I want enemies I have created with "Save As…" to appear in
    the dropdown automatically, so new archetypes are testable with no code
    change.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` is **already the single reusable enemy gym
  scene**: `GymEnemies extends GymFormationScene`, parameterised by
  `init(data?: { enemyKey?: string })`, with the plain-DOM "AI Config" panel
  (sliders, colour inputs, `formationKind`/`shotPattern` selects,
  Respawn/Player toggle, Save/Save As). It is registered under scene key
  `GymEnemies`.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` renders four columns:
  - left — plain scenes;
  - **ENEMIES** — one row per non-boss `EnemyConfig` via
    `discoverEnemyGymEntries()` (`src/utils/enemyGymDiscovery.ts`), each row
    `scene.start('GymEnemies', { enemyKey })`;
  - **Bosses** — "Boss Swarm" (the `boss` config, routed to `GymEnemies` via
    `enemyKey`) and "Boss" (the dedicated multi-phase `GymBoss` scene, booted
    directly via `sceneKey`);
  - **Dev Utilities** — tooling scenes (e.g. `GymCurveSequencer`).
- No enemy-type selector exists in the panel today.
- Seed configs: `scout diver tank phaser swarm boss asteroid harvester march
  capturer ghost-chase ghost-ambush ghost-flank ghost-wander grunt raider`
  (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`), plus any user "Save As…" entries in storage.

## Desired change

1. **Rename the single enemy gym scene** `GymEnemies` →
   **`GymFodderEnemies`** (class, file `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts`,
   scene key `GymFodderEnemies`, and every string/import reference), keeping
   its existing behaviour and panel. The name signals that this scene is the
   *fodder* (non-boss) enemy gym.
2. **Add an enemy selector dropdown** to the AI Config panel — a single
   `<select>` listing every **non-boss** `EnemyConfig`, resolved dynamically
   from the config store (`loadAllEnemyConfigs()` / `listEnemyConfigKeys()`) so
   seed and "Save As…" entries both appear. The selection is seeded from the
   scene's active enemy key. `boss` is deliberately **excluded** (the boss has
   its own entry — see 3).
3. **Rebuild the scene on selection change** (the core requirement):
   destroy every live formation entity and any player bullets, load the
   selected `EnemyConfig`, rebuild the formation config / entity factory /
   bullet dispatch, **reload every other panel control** from the selected
   config (discarding unsaved edits from the previous enemy), and spawn the
   new formation through the shared clean-slate seam
   (`GymFormationScene.respawnFormation()`), i.e. the same path the existing
   **Respawn** button already uses.
4. **Simplify the index to match:**
   - the ENEMIES column becomes a **single "Fodder Enemies" row** that boots
     `GymFodderEnemies` bare (dropdown default = `scout`); the per-config
     fodder rows are removed;
   - the **Bosses column and its header are removed**, and the dedicated
     **`GymBoss` "Boss" row is relocated into the ENEMIES column** (the
     redundant "Boss Swarm" `boss`-config row is dropped);
   - keyboard focus order (Tab/arrows/Enter) and ESC-to-menu continue to work
     across the revised layout.
5. Preserve the existing wave-timeout semantics (non-boss keys get the shared
   wave timeout; the `boss` key remains timeout-free) and all gym↔game parity
   conventions — reuse the shared core seams, do not fork gameplay code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Rename** `GymEnemies` → `GymFodderEnemies`: `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts`
      exports `GymFodderEnemies` registered under scene key `GymFodderEnemies`;
      no production code routes to or imports a scene key/class named
      `GymEnemies` (historical documentation notes may retain the old name with
      a "formerly" note).
- [ ] **Dropdown present and dynamic**: the AI Config panel renders exactly one
      enemy `<select>` whose options are the non-boss config keys (seed +
      storage), including a newly "Save As…" key after re-boot, with the active
      key selected; no hard-coded key list.
- [ ] **Selection change rebuilds the scene**: dispatching `change` on the
      dropdown destroys all previously spawned entities (old references no
      longer live) and player bullets, then spawns the selected enemy type with
      its configured `count`/formation — asserted for at least two different
      keys in a boot test.
- [ ] **Panel resync**: after a selection change every slider/colour/select
      reflects the new enemy's persisted config, and a subsequent slider edit
      applies to the newly selected enemy (`currentConfig.key` updated).
- [ ] **Index layout**: `GymIndex`'s ENEMIES column contains exactly the single
      fodder row (booting `GymFodderEnemies`) plus the dedicated `GymBoss`
      row; no per-enemy rows, no Bosses column/header, no "Boss Swarm" row;
      updated `GymIndex` tests assert the new columns/labels and keyboard focus
      order.
- [ ] **Regression coverage**: existing `GymEnemies` test coverage (per-seed
      formations, panel controls, respawn, power-ups, parity) is migrated to
      `GymFodderEnemies` and passes.
- [ ] **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes
      (`npm test`), including gym-parity/equivalence guards.
- [ ] **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes — at
      minimum `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§1.1 single reusable
      gym scene, §8.5 gym surface/editor panel, index-layout description) and
      any other docs referencing `GymEnemies` or the index columns — plus code
      comments.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity** (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  §5.1): an enabled gameplay object must run the same code in a gym and in the
  game; the dropdown only changes *which* config is active, never gameplay
  behaviour. Reuse `respawnFormation()` / `registerDynamicEntity()` rather than
  re-implementing destroy/spawn.
- **Discovery-driven, no hard-coded lists**: the dropdown options come from the
  config store, exactly as `discoverEnemyGymEntries()` does today.
- **Idempotent / resilient**: missing or corrupt storage must not throw (fall
  back to seed defaults, as `loadEnemyConfig` already does).
- Keep `init({ enemyKey })` supported as an optional deep-link default (useful
  for tests and any future route) unless planning decides otherwise.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (needs producer confirmation):** per answers 1a/2b, the
  "Boss Swarm" `boss`-config row is **removed** and only the dedicated
  `GymBoss` "Boss" row moves into the ENEMIES column, with the Bosses column
  and header deleted. The `boss` archetype is therefore no longer selectable
  from the fodder dropdown. If the intent was to *retain* the "Boss Swarm" row
  inside the ENEMIES column, only step 4 changes.
- **Rename blast radius:** the string/class `GymEnemies` is referenced in
  ~20 files (comments, test harness `bootCombatGymEnemies`, parity tests,
  fixtures). Grep-sweep and rename carefully; keep the parity/equivalence
  guards green.
- **Risks:** stale-entity crash on scene restart (cf. AH-0MTPLHLZ3006MOC4) —
  the dropdown rebuild must reuse the shared respawn/registration seam to
  avoid re-introducing it; focus-manager ordering changes when a column is
  removed.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no last-selection persistence, no favourite/pinning,
  no per-enemy dropdown grouping, no dropdown for boss archetypes — record any
  such idea as a separate linked work item, not in this change.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — rename to `GymFodderEnemies.ts`; add the
  enemy `<select>` row + selection-change handler and panel resync.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts` — rename/update; add dropdown rebuild
  tests.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — single fodder row; remove Bosses column; relocate
  `GymBoss` row; update column constants.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` — update column/label/focus assertions.
- `src/utils/enemyGymDiscovery.ts` — dropdown enumeration now belongs in the
  scene; repurpose or retire (and its tests).
- `src/test/powerUpTestFixtures.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — `bootCombatGymEnemies`
  harness references the old scene.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts`, `src/scenes/core/*` (parity/equivalence tests),
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`, `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` — comment/string
  references to `GymEnemies`.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §1.1, §8.5 and index layout.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What happens to the GymIndex ENEMIES column?**
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): **1a** — replace the per-enemy rows with
  a single row that boots the single enemy gym scene; **and also move the bosses
  into the enemies column**; **name the single scene `GymFodderEnemies`**.
- **Q2 — What does the dropdown list, and does the Bosses column change?**
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): **2b** — all configs **except `boss`**;
  remove the redundant "Boss Swarm" config row (see Q1 for the boss row
  relocation).
- **Q3 — On dropdown change, what happens to the rest of the panel and running
  state?**
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): **3a** — reload every panel control
  from the newly selected enemy's persisted config (discarding unsaved edits),
  clear player bullets and run the shared clean `respawnFormation()` path; no
  change to wave-timeout semantics.
- Sources: interactive operator replies in the intake session. Related work
  identified via Worklog search (see the automated related-work report appended
  below / in the work item).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUQUOZBC00016LQ** – F1: AOE core infrastructure (descriptor + dispatch) (completed)
- **AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44** – Massive Explosions and Fireworks on Victory (completed)
- **AH-0MTCNZ7DN0049K73** – Scene-level tests: GymPowerUps via gameHarness (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, active, add, agents, already (+345 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: active, add, agents, already, also (+328 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: active, add, already, also, always (+310 more)

# Reverse nose retro-thruster VFX

**Parent:** AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG — Add a reverse thruster to the Asteroids ship control scheme
**Covers parent AC:** AC4 (reverse VFX)

## Goal

Show a dedicated forward-facing nose retro-thruster flame while the ship reverses, using the
existing animated-flame model, so the reverse thrust direction is readable from the ship itself.

## Context

`Player.ts` defines `ASTEROIDS_ENGINES` (`main` rear + `leftSide`/`rightSide` forward-side ports) and
animates a flame per port via `_updateFlames`. `getEngineActivity` in `AsteroidsModel` selects the
firing engines per key (AH-0MTFORPJ2003RWWQ). The nose port must follow the same data-driven model and
rotate with the hull.

## Desired change

- Add a `nose` `EnginePortDef` to `ASTEROIDS_ENGINES`: positioned forward on the hull with a
  forward-facing outward normal so the exhaust shoots forward, rotating with the hull.
- Return the `nose` engine from `AsteroidsModel.getEngineActivity` when `reverse` is held and the
  reverse thruster is enabled.
- Render/animate the nose flame through the existing per-port flame path; only firing engines drawn.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Reverse thrust renders a dedicated forward-facing nose retro-thruster flame that grows and decays using the existing animated-flame model and rotates with the hull (AC4).
- [ ] `getEngineActivity` returns the nose engine only while reverse is held with the reverse thruster enabled, alongside the other firing engines.
- [ ] Only engines that are firing are drawn: the nose flame is absent when reversing is disabled or when no reverse key is held.

## Dependencies

- Depends on: Reverse input and physics in the shared movement model.

## Test-first

Write the failing tests for this slice first, then implement until the whole suite is green before committing (the implement workflow requires build + tests to pass on every commit, so tests land with the code in this child).

**Key Files:**

- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `ASTEROIDS_ENGINES` nose port, flame draw/animation wiring.
- `src/utils/movementModel.ts` — `getEngineActivity` returns the nose engine while reversing.
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/utils/movementModel.test.ts` — engine-selection and flame tests.

# Intake Brief — New power-ups and weapons from classic arcade games

## Problem statement

AI_Hell's power-up catalogue (8 types: Shield, Bomb, Speed Boost, Phase Shift,
Teleport, Extra Life, Magnet, Mineral Scoop) and weapon catalogue (permanent
Cannon plus Spread, Dual, Rapid and the AOE family Nova, Mortar, Arc) are
coherent and well-tuned, but they were grown organically rather than
deliberately mining the **classic arcade era** for signature, instantly
recognisable player abilities. This epic researches that era and turns the
best candidates into implementable work items, so the game grows a distinctive
"arcade homage" arsenal without ad-hoc, un-scoped power-up or weapon requests.

The sibling enemy epic (AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52, "New enemies from classic arcade
games") established the pattern this epic mirrors: a shared research catalogue
plus one full-lifecycle child work item per selected concept.

## Users

- **As the game designer**, I want a researched, curated catalogue of classic
  arcade power-up and weapon behaviours adapted to AI_Hell's neon-vector rules,
  so new arsenal work starts from a clear design brief rather than a one-line
  wish.
- **As an implementing agent/developer**, I want each selected power-up/weapon
  to have its own work item with a user story, testable ACs, predicted key
  files and a plan that follows the existing catalogue/level-curve conventions,
  so I can implement it without re-deriving the design.
- **As the producer**, I want the candidates that were considered but not
  selected recorded, so the arsenal can be expanded later without redoing the
  research.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to collect new arcade-inspired weapons and power-ups
  that feel distinct from the existing nine weapons and eight power-ups, so
  runs stay varied as the roster grows.
- As a **developer**, I want every new item to plug into the existing
  catalogue, level-curve, drop-weight, icon, AOE and gym-parity seams, so
  adding it does not fork the game/gym code paths.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A research document `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` exists and catalogues at least 5 and at most 8 selected classic-arcade power-up/weapon concepts, recording for each its source game, original behaviour, adaptation to AI_Hell's neon-vector code-drawn arena, selection rationale, and whether it is a power-up or a weapon.
- The research document includes a considered-but-not-selected section listing the remaining candidates from the research pool, each with a one-line reason for deferral, so the range can be expanded later.
- One child work item exists per selected concept, each containing a user story, measurable and testable acceptance criteria including unit tests, predicted key files, and a full-lifecycle plan (catalogue entry + level-curve variables + code + tests + gym parity + docs), and each child references this epic and the research document.
- Each selected weapon's design notes specify its `WeaponId`/`WEAPON_CATALOGUE` entry, its fire subdivision on the shared 80 BPM beat grid, whether it needs a new `AoEDescriptor`/trigger or a new shared combat-core dispatch seam, and its `weaponLevels.ts` upgrade variables.
- Each selected power-up's design notes specify its `PowerUpId`/`POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` entry, its timed/stored/permanent semantics, its `powerUpLevels.ts` upgrade variables, its code-drawn icon, and its `powerUpWeights` drop weight.

## Constraints

- **Neon-vector aesthetic, code-drawn graphics only** — no external art assets
  (GDD §7.2); every new drop needs a code-drawn icon in `src/powerups/icons.ts`.
- **Gym↔game parity** — an enabled gameplay object must run the same code in a
  gym and the game; shared behaviour lives in `src/scenes/core/`. Enforced by
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the gym-parity docs
  assertion (AGENTS.md).
- **Weapons are cumulative and timed (10 s)** and must fire on an exact
  subdivision or whole-beat multiple of the shared 80 BPM beat grid
  (`src/utils/beat.ts`, AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- **Power-ups follow the temporary/permanent split** — a field pickup adds a
  temporary level tied to the item's timed window; a hold-full reward grants a
  permanent level (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, AH-0MUX802450085VZZ).
- **Every item must carry a level curve** — a new weapon needs
  `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS` entries (`src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`); a new power-up
  needs `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` entries (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`), using
  the one shared curve (`src/utils/curve.ts`). No power-up or weapon is exempt.
- **Data-driven catalogue + drop weights** — items are entries in
  `src/powerups/types.ts` / `src/utils/weapons.ts` plus relative weights in
  `src/core/rules.ts`; tuning is data, not code.
- **"Enemies are the bullets" design** (GDD §2.4) and **no enemy–enemy
  collisions** (GDD §2.6) constrain any power-up that changes enemy behaviour
  (e.g. a Pac-Man-style frightened state).
- **Behaviours must fit a top-down free-2D arena** — the brief must state how
  each concept is translated (or note where translation is not faithful).
- **Balance guardrail** — new items must not trivialise the run or make the
  existing catalogue redundant; coverage and drop weight are part of the design
  notes.
- **Scope is research + design + child-item creation.** This epic does not
  itself implement the items; each selected concept's implementation is its own
  child work item.

- **Gym surface**: `GymWeapons` (weapon drops + help overlay),

- **Precedent**: the sibling epic's `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` and its

  research catalogue and its automated check.
- GDD §8 "Future Scope" already anticipates roster expansion; §4.4 documents

## Desired change

Produce researched, ready-to-implement power-up and weapon concepts drawn from
classic arcade games and capture each as a scoped full-lifecycle child work
item, with a shared research document acting as the catalogue and the record of
deferred candidates.

**Proposed candidate pool** (research selects 5–8; the rest go in the
"considered but not selected" section). Each candidate is anchored to the
classic-arcade source game named. The pool intentionally mixes weapons and
power-ups.

Weapons:

- Galaga — "Dual Fighter" escort/companion ship that trails the player and
  fires alongside it.
- Gradius — "Options"/"Multiple" orbiting satellites that each fire along the
  ship's heading.
- R-Type — piercing "Wave Laser" that passes through enemies (uses the
  catalogued `piercing` upgrade variable).
- Centipede — ricocheting shot that bounces off arena edges (uses the
  catalogued `bounces` upgrade variable).
- Defender / Robotron 2084 — "Smart Bomb" screen-wide enemy-clearing pulse.
- Missile Command — cluster/MIRV missile that splits into multiple warheads
  (uses the catalogued `split` upgrade variable).
- Tempest — "Superzapper" screen pulse that damages all enemies once.
- Sinistar — stored-ammo "Sinibomb" consumable (may need a new stored-ammo
  seam).

Power-ups:

- Pac-Man — "Power Pellet" that frightens enemies (they flee and stop firing)
  for a timed window.
- Space Invaders — "Mystery UFO" bonus pickup (concentrated score/minerals).
- Defender — "Smart Bomb" power-up (clears enemy bullets and damages all
  enemies once).
- Gradius — "Force Field"/reflector that bounces enemy bullets back.
- Galaga — player-side tractor/"Repulsor" that pushes enemies and bullets away.
- Frogger — "Super Leap"/invulnerability window across a hazard lane.
- Asteroids — "Decoy"/"Clay Pigeon" that draws enemy fire for a timed window.
- Gauntlet — "Potion" burst that clears nearby threats on pickup.

*(Every candidate in the pool is recorded in the research document; only 5–8
become child work items. If fewer than 5 survive the engine-constraint review,
a smaller selection is acceptable, and the shortfall is recorded with reasons.)*

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: the research could expand indefinitely. Mitigation —
  cap selection at 5–8 this round; record all other candidates in the deferred
  section. Extra opportunities become linked work items, not scope.
- **Balance risk**: a screen-clearing power-up (Smart Bomb / Superzapper) or a
  piercing/ricochet weapon could trivialise runs or eclipse Nova/Mortar/Arc.

  and how it stays distinct from the existing catalogue.
- **Pipeline-fit risk**: some concepts (companion ship, orbiting options,

  enemy behaviour and must stay gym↔game identical (shared core, not per-scene).
- **Assumption**: "classic arcade era" means the coin-op era of the late 1970s
  to mid-1980s, anchored by the same games the enemy epic used (Space Invaders,
